note: Canonical statistical unit vocabulary for CENSUS. Every estimate must declare exactly one unit. Arithmetic between incompatible units is prohibited without explicit conversion. See CENSUS §46-56.

units.label: Active Energy Performance Contract engagement
units.definition: One executed Energy Performance Contract between one ESCO or retrofit contractor and one building owner or operator, currently in its contractual measurement and verification period. Covers one building or campus. Counted as STOCK at a reference date. One enterprise may have multiple EPC engagements; they must not be collapsed to enterprise count without explicit evidence on average contracts/enterprise.
aggregationRules: Do not assume 1 ESCO = 1 EPC engagement. ESCOs manage many simultaneous contracts.
Do not assume 1 building = 1 EPC. Large campuses may have multiple EPCs.
units.sourceDefinition: No official EU-wide EPC register exists as of 2026. Counts must be derived from ESCO market revenue data or national EED Article 5 implementation reports.

units.label: EPC M&V settlement event (annual flow)
units.definition: One instance of a performance settlement calculation attempt under an active EPC, occurring once per contractual measurement period (typically annually). Each active EPC generates exactly one settlement event per period. Dispute events are a subset.
aggregationRules: Annual settlement events = active EPCs × settlement events per EPC per year. Do not double-count the base EPC stock as the event flow.
units.notes: DOGFOOD A. Stock × frequency = flow. Frequency = 1 settlement/year per active EPC under most IPMVP protocols.

units.label: ESCO enterprise (EU-27)
units.definition: One legal enterprise classified as an Energy Service Company that operates performance-based energy contracts. Counted by enterprise (not by establishment or employee). An ESCO managing 50 active EPCs is ONE enterprise.
aggregationRules: An ESCO enterprise may have multiple establishments. Do not count establishments as enterprises.
units.sourceDefinition: EUROACE/EFIEES member definitions. Eurostat NACE D35.1 or M71 depending on primary activity classification.
units.notes: DOGFOOD A. Not the billing unit. The EPC engagement is the billing unit.

units.label: Building owner / operator enterprise (EU-27)
units.definition: One legal enterprise that owns or operates commercial or public-sector buildings and has entered at least one EPC. May include municipalities, real estate companies, hospitals, universities.
units.sourceDefinition: Eurostat NACE L68, O84, P85, Q86 depending on sector.
units.notes: DOGFOOD A. Counter-party unit. Not billing unit.

units.label: High-stakes B2B procurement decision event (EU-27+UK)
units.definition: One distinct procurement decision by one buyer organization for one product or service category where: (a) the purchase value exceeds EUR 50,000, (b) the product is a capital item, regulated material, or complex B2B software, and (c) independent evidence of performance materially affects the decision. One enterprise generates multiple such events per year. Events, not organizations, are counted.
aggregationRules: Do not collapse to enterprise count without evidence on events/enterprise/year distribution.
Do not count the same purchase decision in multiple sector buckets.
units.sourceDefinition: No official source counts qualifying procurement events directly. Must be derived from enterprise counts × assumed events/enterprise/year.
units.notes: DOGFOOD B (FactBounty, idea-061). Revenue unit is bounty transaction, not procurement event. Conversion ratio required.

units.label: B2B buyer enterprise (EU-27+UK, 50+ employees)
units.definition: One legal enterprise with 50+ employees that makes qualifying high-stakes B2B procurement decisions. The denominator for exposure/eligibility counts. Not the revenue unit.
units.sourceDefinition: Eurostat SBS table sbs_sc_ovw: enterprises by size class × NACE. 50+ employees = size classes 50-249 + 250+.
units.notes: DOGFOOD B. Stock denominator. Flow (events) derived from stock × frequency assumption.

units.label: FactBounty platform bounty transaction
units.definition: One buyer-funded product question bounty posted and fulfilled on the FactBounty platform. The revenue unit. One procurement decision event may generate zero or multiple bounty transactions depending on buyer behavior.
aggregationRules: Do not assume 1 procurement event = 1 bounty. Conversion rate is unknown and Mercury-owned.
units.notes: DOGFOOD B. Mercury must validate conversion rate from procurement event to bounty transaction.

units.label: Registered grid flexibility site (EU-27+UK)
units.definition: One physical industrial or commercial site formally registered with a grid operator or aggregator to participate in a grid flexibility market (demand response, balancing mechanism, FCR, aFRR, etc.) with at least 1 MW flexible load capacity. Counted as STOCK at a reference date. One enterprise may operate multiple flexibility sites.
aggregationRules: Do not sum sites to enterprises without evidence on sites/enterprise ratio.
Do not equate registered flexibility capacity (MW) to site count.
units.sourceDefinition: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform: Balancing Service Provider registrations. National grid operator registries (Ofgem, BNetzA, RTE, ELIA).
units.notes: DOGFOOD C (FlexCovenant, idea-434 / BatteryDuty, idea-432). The commercial account unit may be the aggregator enterprise, not the site. Mercury must confirm.

units.label: Active flexibility aggregator enterprise (EU-27+UK)
units.definition: One legal enterprise that aggregates flexible load from multiple sites and submits combined bids to grid operators. Counted as STOCK. One aggregator manages 10-50+ sites typically.
aggregationRules: Do not sum aggregator enterprises + site counts as separate customers — they share a hierarchy.
units.sourceDefinition: TERRAIN importanceSignals: estimated 200+ aggregators in EU27. ACER market monitoring report.
units.notes: DOGFOOD C. Potential commercial account unit — subject to Mercury confirmation.

units.label: Called grid flexibility activation event
units.definition: One called balancing or demand-response activation at one registered flexibility site, during one settlement period. One site may receive thousands of calls per year under continuous frequency markets (FCR) or tens per year under manual demand response. Counted as annual FLOW.
aggregationRules: Do not sum FCR (continuous, ~8760/year) and manual DR (discrete, ~20/year) events as equivalent problem events — they have structurally different reconciliation loads.
units.sourceDefinition: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform: activated balancing energy by product and period.
units.notes: DOGFOOD C. The settlement-identifier-mismatch problem occurs per event. But severity depends on frequency: high-frequency FCR events each produce small individual disputes; low-frequency manual DR events may produce larger individual disputes.
